cards.back:
uno · dos · tres · cuatro · cinco
seis · siete · ocho · nueve · diez
cards.grammarNote: **Uno** becomes **un** before a masculine noun: **un dado** (one die). Before a feminine noun: **una cara** (one face/side). Numbers 2–10 are invariable (no gender change).

cards.back:
once · doce · trece · catorce · quince
dieciséis · diecisiete · dieciocho · diecinueve · veinte
cards.grammarNote: 11–15 are unique forms. 16–19 combine **diez** + **y** + unit, contracted into one word: **dieciséis** (diez y seis), **diecisiete**, etc. **Veinte** (20) is its own form. The critical D&D roll: **¡Tiré un veinte!** (I rolled a twenty!)

cards.back:
veinte · treinta · cuarenta · cincuenta
sesenta · setenta · ochenta · noventa · cien
cards.grammarNote: 21–29 are written as one word: **veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés…** 31–99 use **y**: **treinta y uno, cuarenta y cinco**. **Cien** = exactly 100; **ciento** is used before other numbers: **ciento cincuenta** (150).

cards.back:
cien(to) · doscientos · trescientos · cuatrocientos · quinientos
seiscientos · setecientos · ochocientos · novecientos · mil
cards.grammarNote: Hundreds 200–900 agree in gender with the noun they modify: **doscientos puntos** (m.) but **doscientas fichas** (f.). Note irregular forms: **quinientos** (500), **setecientos** (700), **novecientos** (900) — not **cincocientos** etc.

**Saqué** = I got/rolled — preterite yo of **sacar** (c→qu before e: saqué). **Tiré** = I threw/rolled — preterite yo of **tirar** (regular -ar: tiré). Both verbs are used colloquially for rolling dice in Spanish D&D communities.

cards.front: I need a six or higher.
cards.grammarNote: **o más** = or more/higher — **más** (more) functions as a comparison word. Alternative: **Necesito un seis como mínimo** (I need at least a six — literally 'as a minimum'). **como mínimo** / **al menos** = at least.

**cincuenta** = 50 (invariable — numbers from 2 upward don't change for gender). **Tengo** is the irregular yo form of **tener** (to have). Useful D&D health phrases: **Me quedan diez puntos de vida** (I only have ten hit points left — lit. 'there remain to me ten').

cards.back: El dragón hace veinticinco puntos de daño.
cards.grammarNote: **hace** = deals/does (él/ella present of **hacer**, irregular yo: **hago**). **Puntos de daño** = damage points — the standard D&D phrase in Spanish. **veinticinco** = 25 (written as one word, like all 21–29).

cards.back:
el d4 · el d6 · el d8 · el d10 · el d12 · el d20 · el d100
OR: dado de cuatro caras, dado de seis caras…
cards.grammarNote: Spanish D&D communities often borrow the English abbreviations (d4, d6, d20) directly. The descriptive form is **dado de [number] caras** (die of [number] faces). All are masculine: **el dado**, **los dados**.

cards.front:
Ordinal numbers 1st–10th
(for rounds, levels, dungeon floors)
cards.back:
primero/a · segundo/a · tercero/a · cuarto/a · quinto/a
sexto/a · séptimo/a · octavo/a · noveno/a · décimo/a
cards.grammarNote: Ordinals agree in gender: **el primer nivel** (the first level — **primero** drops -o before masculine nouns), **la tercera planta** (the third floor). Above 10th, cardinal numbers are commonly used instead: **el nivel once** (level eleven).

cards.back: El explorador de Jeffrey es nivel ocho.
cards.grammarNote: **es nivel ocho** — in D&D, level is treated as an identity characteristic (ser). Note: no article before **nivel** in this construction: **es nivel ocho** (not 'el nivel ocho'). Compare: **Estamos en el nivel ocho** (We are on level eight — estar for location).

cards.front: I rolled a fourteen for initiative.
cards.grammarNote: **catorce** = 14 (unique form, not **diezycuatro**). **de iniciativa** = for initiative — **de** links the roll to its purpose. Full D&D initiative sequence: **Todos tiran iniciativa** → **¿Cuánto sacaste?** (What did you roll?) → **Saqué un catorce** (I got a fourteen).

cards.front: That's eight plus four, so twelve total.
cards.back: Son ocho más cuatro, entonces doce en total.
cards.grammarNote: Math language in Spanish: **más** = plus, **menos** = minus, **por** = times/multiplied by, **entre** = divided by. **Son** (from **ser**) is used for sums and totals: **Tres más tres son seis** (Three plus three is six). **en total** = in total / altogether.

cards.front: We found three hundred gold coins.
cards.grammarNote: **trescientas** — note the feminine form agreeing with **monedas** (coins, feminine): **trescientos** (m.) vs **trescientas** (f.). All hundreds from 200–900 have masculine and feminine forms. **monedas de oro** = gold coins (literally 'coins of gold').
